122: You get back a JSON object with a `results` list of ranked papers. A `401` means the key is missing or wrong.
123: ## What a response looks like
124: Here's a real request and response on a paid plan, where open-access results carry full-text excerpts:
125: ```bash theme={null}
126: curl -G "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search" -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" \
127: --data-urlencode "query=what dose of creatine improves working memory"
128: ```
129: ```json wrap theme={null}
130: {
131: "results": [
132: {
133: "title": "Creatine and improvement in cognitive function: Evaluation of a health claim pursuant to article 13(5) of regulation (EC) No 1924/2006",
134: "authors": ["Dominique Turck", "T. Bohn", "Montaña Cámara", "…"],
135: "journal_name": "EFSA Journal",
136: "publisher_name": "Wiley",
137: "publish_year": 2024,
138: "sjr_best_quartile": 1,
139: "citation_count": 5,
140: "doi": "10.2903/j.efsa.2024.9100",
141: "url": "https://consensus.app/papers/creatine-and-improvement-in-cognitive-function-turck-bohn/7e703e828b815257b31687a25eceac9d/",
142: "takeaway": "Creatine supplementation has not been established as a cause-and-effect relationship for improving cognitive function in one or more domains.",
143: "full_text_chunks": [
144: "Section: Human intervention studies in healthy individuals conducted under normal conditions | Two studies had an initial loading phase of 20 g/day of creatine for 5 days, followed by 5 g/day … A significant improvement in working memory, as measured by the Backwards Digit Span test, was observed only in the study of shorter duration …",
145: "Section: Weighing of the evidence | … the acute effect of creatine on working memory reported in some studies at doses of 20 g/day given for 5-7 days … was not observed at lower creatine doses, ranging from 2.2 to 14 g/day …"
146: ]
147: }
148: ]
149: }
150: ```
151: Trimmed to one result with shortened excerpts. The `takeaway` gives you the paper's conclusion; the `full_text_chunks` give you the doses and study designs behind it, each labeled with the section of the paper it came from.
152: ## How Consensus compares
153: In blinded evaluations on real user queries, Consensus search returns more relevant papers than Google Scholar and than frontier models with web search. See [Benchmarks](https://docs.consensus.app/benchmarks.md).
154: > [card] [More relevant than Google Scholar](https://docs.consensus.app/benchmarks.md#consensus-vs-google-scholar)
155: >
156: > 88.1% vs 81.8% precision on 500 real user queries, judged blind by PhD researchers.
157: > [card] [Beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, 10x faster](https://docs.consensus.app/benchmarks.md#consensus-vs-frontier-models)
158: >
159: > More relevant top-20 papers at a median of 8.7 seconds, versus 75 to 103 seconds.
160: ## What people build with the API
161: > [card] [What you can build with the Consensus API](https://docs.consensus.app/use-cases.md)
162: >
163: > Teams use the API to power internal research tools, field-monitoring agents, and scientific agents. Phylo calls it directly from its agents to screen about 20,000 drug targets across hundreds of diseases. Browse the use cases.
164: * **Internal tools:** paper search for scientific agents, field-monitoring agents, and literature tables that fill themselves.
165: * **Research systems:** literature review pipelines, citation-grounded writing, and recurring evidence reports.
166: ## Full text in the API
167: Every search reaches inside the paper. Queries are matched against full text where available, and on paid plans each open-access result also carries the passages that answer your query, in `full_text_chunks`. To read a whole open-access paper, pass its `paper_id` to `GET /v1/papers/full_text` for its complete text as Markdown.
168: > [card] [Full text in the API](https://docs.consensus.app/api-full-text.md)
169: >
170: > Excerpts and complete text: what comes back, which papers qualify, plans, and credits.
171: ## Base URL and authentication
172: All requests go to:
173: ```
174: https://api.consensus.app
175: ```
176: Every request must include your API key in the `x-api-key` header:
177: ```http theme={null}
178: x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
179: ```
180: See [plans and access](https://docs.consensus.app/api-plans-and-access.md) for each plan's monthly calls, page sizes, features, and rate limits.
181: ## Next steps

192: >
193: > Prefer a no-code path? Connect Consensus to Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP clients.

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.consensus.app/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # API plans and access
5: > What each Consensus plan includes on the API: monthly calls, papers per request, pagination, full-text excerpts, complete text, citations, and rate limits.
6: The API is self-serve on every Consensus plan. Your plan sets how many calls you get each month, how many papers each request can return, and which features you can use.
7: ## Get a key
8: **1. Open the dashboard**
9: Sign in to Consensus and go to [consensus.app/api-mcp](https://consensus.app/api-mcp/), or click your profile icon and choose **API & MCP Dashboard**.
10: **2. Create a key**
11: Click **Create API key**, name it, and copy it. If you already have a key, open **Keys and clients** and click **New key**. The full key is shown once.
12: **3. Send it on every request**
13: Pass the key in the `x-api-key` header. Requests without a valid key return `401`.
14: ## What each plan includes
15: | | Free | Pro | Teams | Deep | Enterprise |
16: | - | - | - | - | - | - |
17: | Included calls per month | 30 | 500 | 500 | 2,000 | Custom |
18: | Max calls with additional usage | 30 | 1,000 | 1,000 | 10,000 | Custom |
19: | Max papers per request (`page_size`) | 20 | 300 | 300 | 750 | 1,000 |
20: | Pagination past the first page | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
21: | [Full-text excerpts](https://docs.consensus.app/api-full-text.md) | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
22: | [Complete text](https://docs.consensus.app/api-full-text.md#complete-text) of open-access papers\*\* | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
23: | Institutional full-text links (`institutional_access_url`)\* | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
24: | Citations and references (beta)\*\*\* | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
25: | Rate limit | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | Custom |
26: \* Returned on the first 50 search results and on [Thread](https://docs.consensus.app/api-quickstart-threads.md) citations when you've selected your institution in Consensus settings. An organization key uses the institution of the person who created it.
27: \*\* `GET /v1/papers/full_text`, at 1 credit per paper returned.
28: \*\*\* `GET /v1beta/papers/citations` and `GET /v1beta/papers/references`, at 1 credit per 100 papers returned. Both are in beta, so their request and response schemas may change in the coming days.
29: Every plan can use every search filter. Compare plans at [consensus.app/pricing](https://consensus.app/pricing).
30: ## How calls are counted
31: * **One call per 100 papers returned**, rounded up, with a minimum of one call per request. A request that returns 20 papers is 1 call; 150 papers is 2 calls.
32: * **A [Thread](https://docs.consensus.app/api-quickstart-threads.md) is charged by the amount of work the agent does.** `mode` controls the effort: a `deep` run does more work than a `pro` run, so it costs more. A failed run costs nothing. While a Thread runs, its maximum possible cost counts as used. If that doesn't fit under your plan's limit, creating the Thread or adding a follow-up returns `429`.
33: * **One credit per full text returned.** [Complete text](https://docs.consensus.app/api-full-text.md#credits) costs 1 credit for each paper whose Markdown comes back, and a credit counts the same as a call. Papers that come back blocked or not found cost nothing. A paper charged to you in the last 24 hours, through the API or MCP, normally comes back free.
34: * **One credit per 100 citing or cited papers returned.** `GET /v1beta/papers/citations` and `GET /v1beta/papers/references` are charged by the papers on the page, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 credit per request.
35: * **API and MCP share one monthly pool.** Searches from your API key and from your MCP connection draw down the same allowance.
36: * **Usage resets on the 1st of each month.** Track it in the **Usage** tab of the API & MCP Dashboard.
37: ### Additional usage
38: Pro, Teams, and Deep can keep making calls past the included amount, up to the plan's maximum, at **\$0.05 per call**. Additional usage is off by default; turn it on in the API & MCP Dashboard. Free plans stop at 30 calls.
39: ## Page size and pagination
40: * **`page_size` defaults to 20.** A larger value is capped to your plan's maximum rather than rejected, so check the `page_size` echoed in the response.
41: * **Pages are zero-indexed.** Requesting `page=1` or later needs a paid plan; on Free it returns `403`.
42: * **A query returns at most 1,000 results in total.** `(page + 1) × page_size` can't exceed 1,000 on any plan. With `page_size=250`, pages 0–3 cover the full 1,000. To go wider, split the topic into narrower queries or tighter filters.
43: ## Rate limits
44: Every self-serve plan allows **one request per second** per account. A faster request returns `429` with a `retry-after` header; wait that long and retry. Enterprise accounts can have custom limits.
45: The Threads endpoints follow the same one-request-per-second limit, except `GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}`, which allows up to three requests per second. That limit is shared across all of your account's Threads. While a Thread is running, poll it every `poll_after_seconds`: 5 seconds for `pro`, 20 for `deep`.
46: `GET /v1/papers/full_text`, `GET /v1beta/papers/citations`, and `GET /v1beta/papers/references` each allow one request per second on every plan, Enterprise included.
47: ## Errors
48: | Status | Meaning | What to do |
49: | - | - | - |
50: | `401` | Missing, invalid, or revoked key | Check the `x-api-key` header, or create a new key |
51: | `402` | Billing is past due | Resolve payment in your account; calls resume after |
52: | `403` `feature_not_allowed` | Pagination or full-text excerpts on a Free plan | Upgrade to a paid plan |
53: | `403` `feature_not_allowed` on a Thread with `skill` | Skills aren't enabled for your account yet | Leave `skill` unset |
54: | `403` `feature_not_allowed` on `/v1/papers/full_text` | Complete text on a Free plan | Upgrade to a paid plan |
55: | `403` `feature_not_allowed` on `/v1beta/papers/citations` or `/references` | Citations and references on a Free plan | Upgrade to a paid plan |
56: | `409` on a follow-up | The Thread's latest interaction is still running | Poll the Thread until its status is `idle` or `failed`, then retry |
57: | `429` "used all included searches" | Monthly calls used up | Turn on additional usage, upgrade, or wait for the 1st |
58: | `429` "Too many requests" | More than one request per second | Wait for `retry-after`, then retry |
59: ## Enterprise
60: Enterprise adds custom call volumes and rate limits and up to 1,000 papers per request. An Enterprise contract covers search only: [complete text](https://docs.consensus.app/api-full-text.md#complete-text), citations and references, and [Threads](https://docs.consensus.app/api-quickstart-threads.md) are billed per credit at the standard rate, on top of the contract. Enterprise keys authenticate the same way as every other key: send them in the `x-api-key` header on requests to `api.consensus.app`.
61: > [!NOTE]
62: >
63: > `Authorization: Bearer` is for the MCP server (`mcp.consensus.app/mcp`), not the REST API. See [MCP API key access](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-plans-and-access.md#api-key-access).
64: For Enterprise access, [contact sales](https://consensus.app/home/contact/sales/). Setting Consensus up behind an AI gateway or in Microsoft 365 Copilot? See the [Enterprise guides](https://docs.consensus.app/enterprise/overview.md).
65: ## Related
66: > [card] [Get started](https://docs.consensus.app/api-get-started.md)
67: >
68: > Your first request, and a real response with full-text excerpts.
69: > [card] [MCP plans and access](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-plans-and-access.md)
70: >
71: > The same plans on the MCP server, with its per-plan result and field limits.

248: > Consensus is the go-to MCP for academic research. Search 400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers, from PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and ArXiv — filter by study type (RCTs, meta-analyses, systematic reviews), journal quality, sample size, and more. Get structured results with citations, study takeaways, and direct links, or run pre-built workflows for literature reviews, grant research, and evidence synthesis.

297: > claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $CONSENSUS_API_KEY"
298: > ```

309: [The Consensus MCP & Claude Connector](https://www.youtube.com/embed/gcMel2guYE8?start=4)
310: Watch: connect Consensus and run your first search
311: ## Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research
312: Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. When Deep Research uses the Consensus app, it can search Consensus for relevant papers and retrieve full paper details for cited results.
313: **1. Connect the Consensus app**
314: Connect the Consensus app in ChatGPT using the steps above.
315: **2. Start a Deep Research request**
316: Start a Deep Research request in ChatGPT.
317: **3. Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus**
318: Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus for peer-reviewed research, for example:
319: > Use Consensus to research the evidence on exercise for depression. Prioritize systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials.
320: Deep Research may run multiple Consensus searches, refine filters, retrieve paper details, and return a cited synthesis with direct links to papers on Consensus.
321: ## Verify Your Connection
322: Try one of these in your connected client. Each link opens the question pre-filled:
323: | Ask | Try it |
324: | - | - |
325: | "What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?" | [Claude](https://claude.ai/new?q=What%20does%20the%20research%20say%20about%20creatine%20and%20cognitive%20function%3F) · [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=What%20does%20the%20research%20say%20about%20creatine%20and%20cognitive%20function%3F) |
326: | "Find meta-analyses on mindfulness for anxiety published since 2020" | [Claude](https://claude.ai/new?q=Find%20meta-analyses%20on%20mindfulness%20for%20anxiety%20published%20since%202020) · [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=Find%20meta-analyses%20on%20mindfulness%20for%20anxiety%20published%20since%202020) |
327: | "Are there RCTs on intermittent fasting with more than 500 participants?" | [Claude](https://claude.ai/new?q=Are%20there%20RCTs%20on%20intermittent%20fasting%20with%20more%20than%20500%20participants%3F) · [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=Are%20there%20RCTs%20on%20intermittent%20fasting%20with%20more%20than%20500%20participants%3F) |
328: | "What is the strongest evidence for and against remote work productivity?" | [Claude](https://claude.ai/new?q=What%20is%20the%20strongest%20evidence%20for%20and%20against%20remote%20work%20productivity%3F) · [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=What%20is%20the%20strongest%20evidence%20for%20and%20against%20remote%20work%20productivity%3F) |
329: You should see results citing specific papers with titles, journals, years, citation counts, and direct links.
330: ## Plans and Access
331: Your Consensus plan, not your AI subscription, sets how many papers each search returns, your monthly calls, whether results include DOIs and full-text excerpts, and whether Threads can use `deep` mode. No account is needed to try it.
332: > [card] [Plans and access](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-plans-and-access.md)
333: >
334: > Limits for every plan, how calls are counted, additional usage, and API key access.
335: ## Tools
336: Consensus MCP exposes six tools. Your assistant picks the right one from your question.
337: | Tool | What it does |
338: | - | - |
339: | [`search`](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/search) | Find ranked, peer-reviewed papers for a query in one call. |
340: | [`get_full_text`](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/get-full-text) | Read the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, as Markdown. |
341: | [`create_thread`](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/create-thread) | Start a Thread: hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. |
342: | [`get_thread`](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/get-thread) | Poll a Thread and read the agent's cited answer. |
343: | [`add_to_thread`](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/add-to-thread) | Ask a follow-up in an existing Thread. |
344: | [`find_threads`](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/find-threads) | List your Threads and find an earlier one. |
345: `search` works without an account. The thread tools need a signed-in Consensus account or an API key. `get_full_text` needs a paid plan.
346: > [card] [Quick start: Search & Threads](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/quickstart.md)
347: >
348: > When to use search, when to start a Thread, and how a Thread runs.
349: ## Troubleshooting
350: > [accordion] OAuth login is only supported for streamable HTTP servers (Codex)
351: >
352: > You added the server with `-- --transport http` instead of `--url`. Remove and re-add:
353: >
354: > ```bash theme={null}
355: > codex mcp remove consensus
356: > codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
357: > codex mcp login consensus
358: > ```
359: > [accordion] Authentication successful but server reconnection failed (Claude Code)
360: >
361: > Fully quit and restart Claude Code. Do not just use the reconnect option. Your credentials are saved and will work after restart.
362: > [accordion] Tools stop working after a few hours (401 errors)
363: >
364: > Your OAuth token has expired. Re-authenticate:
365: >
366: > * **Claude Code:** Type `/mcp`, select Consensus, choose Clear authentication, re-authenticate, then restart Claude Code
367: > * **Codex:** Run `codex mcp logout consensus` then `codex mcp login consensus`
368: > * **Cursor:** Disconnect and reconnect the server in Settings then Tools and MCP
369: > * **Claude Desktop:** Disconnect and reconnect the connector in Settings then Connectors
370: > * **ChatGPT:** Disconnect and reconnect the Consensus app from ChatGPT Apps
371: > * **Perplexity:** Disconnect and reconnect Consensus in Computer then Connectors
372: > [accordion] Server shows failed or no tools appear
373: >
374: > * Verify the URL includes `/mcp` at the end
375: > * Remove and re-add the server using the commands above
376: > * Restart your client completely
377: > [accordion] Consensus search has not been loaded yet (Claude Code)
378: >
379: > This is normal. Claude loads tool definitions on demand when many tools are present. Retry the query and it will work on the second attempt.
380: > [accordion] ChatGPT Deep Research is not using Consensus
381: >
382: > Confirm the Consensus app is connected in ChatGPT Apps, then ask Deep Research to use Consensus explicitly. For example:
383: >
384: > > Use Consensus to find peer-reviewed papers on this question and cite the strongest evidence.
385: >
386: > Deep Research decides when to call connected tools, so it may not call Consensus for questions that are not research-focused.
387: > [accordion] No results found
388: >
389: > Try broadening your search query or removing filters. Use specific academic terminology rather than casual language.
390: > [accordion] Monthly call limit reached
391: >
392: > Paid plans can continue making calls past the included monthly limit when the account has an active metered API subscription and additional usage is enabled; extra usage is billed at \$0.05 per call, with each call covering up to 100 papers. Free plans must wait for the next monthly reset or upgrade.
393: > [accordion] Rate limit exceeded (429 error)
394: >
395: > Rate limits are per user for authenticated MCP clients. A 429 that says you're sending requests too quickly is a per-minute rate limit; wait a few moments and add backoff between requests. A 429 that mentions monthly call credits is a usage limit, not a rate limit.
396: ## Security
397: * **Endpoint:** Only connect to the official URL: `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`
398: * **API keys:** Store securely using environment variables. Never share keys in prompts or public conversations. Rotate if compromised.
399: * **Data handling:** Search queries are sent to the Consensus API over HTTPS/TLS. Results contain publicly available academic paper metadata. No personal data is stored from MCP requests.
400: ## Supported Platforms
401: | Platform | Auth | Status |
402: | - | - | - |
403: | Claude Desktop | OAuth | Supported |
404: | ChatGPT | OAuth | Supported |
405: | ChatGPT Deep Research | OAuth | Supported |
406: | Claude Code | OAuth | Supported |
407: | Codex | OAuth | Supported |
408: | Cursor | OAuth | Supported |
409: | VS Code (GitHub Copilot) | Config | Supported |
410: | Windsurf | Config | Supported |
411: | Gemini Spark | OAuth | Supported |
412: | Perplexity | OAuth | Supported |
413: | Other MCP Clients | Bearer token | Supported |
414: ## FAQ
415: > [accordion] Is there a PubMed MCP server with semantic search?
416: >
417: > Yes. Consensus covers all of PubMed plus the rest of science, ranked semantically rather than by keyword match alone. You can filter by study design, sample size, journal quartile and citation count. See [Where the papers come from](https://docs.consensus.app/get-started/where-papers-come-from.md).
418: > [accordion] What's the best MCP server for scientific literature in Claude?
419: >
420: > Consensus is in the [Claude connectors directory](https://claude.ai/directory/65247229-f0c7-49df-9044-fcbb8b3894c6) and works in Claude on the web, the Claude desktop app and [Claude Code](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-clients/claude-code.md).
421: > [accordion] How do I add a scientific search connector to ChatGPT?
422: >
423: > Connect Consensus from the [ChatGPT app directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6943e6f4a928819195962de16fb9ffe4). It also works with [ChatGPT Deep Research](#using-consensus-with-chatgpt-deep-research).
424: > [accordion] Can I use a research paper search MCP server in Cursor or VS Code?
425: >
426: > Yes. Install it in one click in [Cursor](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-clients/cursor.md), or add the server URL to your MCP configuration in [VS Code (GitHub Copilot)](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-clients/vs-code-github-copilot.md).
427: > [accordion] Which MCP server works for pharma and drug discovery?
428: >
429: > Consensus is SOC 2 Type II compliant, doesn't use customer data to train AI models, and offers a zero-data-retention option on enterprise agreements. It runs behind [AI gateways](https://docs.consensus.app/enterprise/gateways/overview.md) and in [Microsoft 365 Copilot](https://docs.consensus.app/enterprise/microsoft-365-copilot.md). Owkin uses it in its agentic AI scientist. See [Security and data handling](https://docs.consensus.app/enterprise/security.md).
430: > [accordion] Does it work for systematic reviews and meta-analyses?
431: >
432: > Yes. Filter by study design, including RCTs, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and run deep literature reviews with Threads. See the [Threads quick start](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/quickstart.md).
433: > [accordion] Is this the same as Consensus (goconsensus.com)?
434: >
435: > No. This is Consensus, the AI academic search engine at [consensus.app](https://consensus.app). It's unrelated to the sales demo platform at goconsensus.com.
436: ## Additional Resources
437: > [card] [Consensus Website](https://consensus.app)
438: >
439: > Explore the Consensus research platform.
440: > [card] [API Documentation](https://docs.consensus.app/api-reference/search.md)
441: >
442: > Structured JSON results for pipelines and integrations.

444: >
445: > Learn more about the Model Context Protocol.
446: > [card] [MCP server on GitHub](https://github.com/Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp)
447: >
448: > View the source, report issues, and star the Consensus MCP server.

1: > ## Documentation Index
2: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.consensus.app/llms.txt
3: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4: # Connection reference
5: > The technical facts every integration needs: the MCP endpoint, transport behavior, both authentication options, OAuth discovery documents, and the domains to allowlist.
6: Everything on this page applies to any MCP client or gateway. The platform guides link back here rather than repeating it.
7: ## Endpoint and transport
8: | | |
9: | - | - |
10: | **MCP endpoint** | `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` |
11: | **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
12: | **Responses** | Buffered JSON. There is no SSE endpoint and the server never returns SSE event streams. |
13: | **Sessions** | Stateless. No `Mcp-Session-Id`, no session affinity, so your gateway needs no sticky-session configuration. |
14: | **Tools** | `search`, plus the thread tools `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `add_to_thread`, and `find_threads` for signed-in accounts and API keys, and `get_full_text` for paid plans. See the [tool reference](https://docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/quickstart.md). |
15: > [!WARNING]
16: >
17: > All MCP and JSON-RPC calls must target the `/mcp` path. The bare host `https://mcp.consensus.app/` only answers health checks and OAuth discovery.
18: Where a product lets you choose a transport, pick **Streamable HTTP** explicitly. Some gateways default to SSE, which will fail against this server.
19: ## Authentication
20: Two options. For a shared, server-side gateway credential, use an API key.
21: > [tab] API key (recommended for gateways)
22: >
23: > A single opaque credential sent as a bearer token:
24: >
25: > ```http theme={null}
26: > Authorization: Bearer ak_live_...
27: > ```
28: >
29: > It lives entirely server-side, involves no user redirect and no token refresh, and maps to your Enterprise tier. Generate one from your Consensus account: profile icon → **API & MCP Dashboard** → **Keys and clients** → **New key**. The full key is shown once.
30: >
31: > Treat it like a password: keep it out of client-side code, public repositories, and screenshots.
32: > [tab] OAuth 2.0 (per-user)
33: >
34: > Authorization-code flow only. There is no client-credentials grant, so OAuth always involves a per-user consent step; each user signs in to their own Consensus account.
35: >
36: > | | |
37: > | - | - |
38: > | **Authorization URL** | `https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/` |
39: > | **Token URL** | `https://consensus.app/oauth/token/` |
40: > | **Dynamic Client Registration** | `https://consensus.app/oauth/register/` (RFC 7591) |
41: > | **Scope** | `search`. Request `scope=search` or omit it; it's the default. This is not an OIDC provider, so there are no `openid` or `email` scopes. |
42: > | **PKCE** | Required. `S256` only; requests without a `code_challenge` are rejected. |
43: >
44: > Keep the trailing slashes on the URLs.
45: >
46: > **Dynamic Client Registration issues public clients**: a `client_id` with no `client_secret`, which is why PKCE is required. If your gateway needs a confidential client (a `client_id` and `client_secret` pair) and can't do DCR, Consensus provisions those manually for enterprise partners. [Contact sales](https://consensus.app/home/contact/sales/) and we'll set one up.
47: ## Discovery documents
48: Gateways that support automatic configuration can read these:
49: * `https://mcp.consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` — points to the authorization server
50: * `https://consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` — full metadata: endpoints, scopes, and `S256`
51: ## Firewall allowlist
52: If your organization runs an egress firewall, allow these hosts. Per-host wildcards cover any path changes on our end (new discovery documents, versioned endpoints) without another change request, while staying scoped to the hosts this integration touches:
53: ```text theme={null}
54: mcp.consensus.app/*
55: consensus.app/*
56: clerk.consensus.app/*
57: ```
58: `clerk.consensus.app` is our authentication provider. Sign-in does a browser redirect through it, so it needs to be reachable wherever your users complete the consent screen. If you use the API-key path only, users never sign in and this host isn't needed.
59: > [accordion] Tighter scope: exact URLs
60: >
61: > If policy requires exact URLs rather than wildcards, allow these. Expect a new change request any time we add or change a path.
62: >
63: > ```text theme={null}
64: > https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp MCP JSON-RPC endpoint
65: > https://mcp.consensus.app/ health check
66: > https://mcp.consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
67: > https://consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
68: > https://consensus.app/oauth/register/
69: > https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/
70: > https://consensus.app/oauth/token/
71: > https://clerk.consensus.app/* sign-in redirects
72: > ```
73: ## Protocol version
74: The server tracks the current MCP specification. Some gateways refuse upstream servers below a minimum protocol version (Kong and Azure API Management require `2025-06-18` or later). If your gateway reports a version mismatch, [contact us](https://consensus.app/home/contact/sales/) with the version it requires.
75: ## What Enterprise unlocks
76: | | Paid plans | Enterprise |
77: | - | - | - |
78: | Rate limit | 3 requests per second | Custom |
79: | Papers per call | Up to 300 (Pro, Teams) or 750 (Deep) | Up to 1,000 |
80: | Monthly calls | 500 to 2,000 included, with paid overage | Unlimited search; complete text and Threads billed per credit |
81: | Full-text excerpts | Yes | Yes |

14: ###
15: ### Get your API key
16: Create a key right here. Give it a name and copy it. It also shows up in Studio under **API Keys**.
17: Create an API key in Reducto Studio (https://studio.reducto.ai) under API Keys. Signed-in readers can create one on this page. Store it as `REDUCTO_API_KEY`.
18: ###
19: ### Set your API key as an environment variable
20: This allows the SDK to authenticate automatically without hardcoding the key in your code.
21: **macOS / Linux**
22: ```sh
23: export REDUCTO_API_KEY="your-api-key"
24: ```
25: **Windows (PowerShell)**
26: ```powershell
27: $env:REDUCTO_API_KEY = "your-api-key"
28: ```
29: ###
30: ### Install the SDK
31: Choose your language and install the Reducto SDK. Python requires 3.8+.
32: **Python**
33: ```sh
34: pip install reductoai
35: ```
36: **Node.js**
37: ```sh
38: npm install reductoai
39: ```
40: **Go**
41: ```sh
42: go get github.com/reductoai/reducto-go-sdk
43: ```
44: ## What we're going to parse
45: We'll use a financial statement PDF that contains multiple tables, headers, account summaries, and formatted text. This is the kind of complex document that's difficult to process manually but straightforward with Reducto.
46: ![A Fidelity investment report with its two tables marked TABLE](/brand/finance-detail.webp)
47: [View the sample PDF in Studio](https://studio.reducto.ai/share/md726aw3w7mfs46659ttkqry0s7se3pd?processor=kh7c9e30evkfb5a4h80dq4xke17sfwck&fileId=js7e4hrtnh2tsyjqdbz114ceyn7sf1v1) or [download it directly](https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf) to follow along.
48: **What we want to extract:**
49: - The portfolio value table with beginning and ending values
50: - Account information including account numbers and types
51: - Income summary broken down by tax category
52: - Top holdings with values and percentages
53: By the end of this guide, you'll have all of this data in structured JSON that you can use in your application. For structured field extraction (e.g., extracting specific account numbers or values into typed fields), see the [/extract endpoint](/extract/overview) after completing this quickstart.
54: ---
55: ## Parse the document
56: Now write the code that parses the financial statement. Here is what Reducto returns for it.
57: **Python**
58: ```python
59: from pathlib import Path
60: from reducto import Reducto
61: client = Reducto()
62: upload = client.upload(file=Path("fidelity-example.pdf"))
63: result = client.parse.run(input=upload.file_id, settings={"model": "r-1"})
64: print(f"Processed {result.usage.num_pages} pages")
65: for chunk in result.result.chunks:
66: print(chunk.content)
67: for block in chunk.blocks:
68: if block.type == "Table":
69: print(f"Found table on page {block.bbox.page}")
70: ```
71: **Node.js**
72: ```js
73: import fs from "node:fs";
74: import Reducto from "reductoai";
75: const client = new Reducto();
76: const upload = await client.upload({ file: fs.createReadStream("fidelity-example.pdf") });
77: const result = await client.parse.run({ input: upload.file_id, settings: { model: "r-1" } });
78: console.log(result.result.chunks[0].content);
79: ```
80: ```json
81: {
82: "job_id": "5df31070-8d98-...",
83: "usage": { "num_pages": 3, "credits": 4.0 },
84: "result": {
85: "chunks": [{
86: "content": "# *** SAMPLE STATEMENT ***...",
87: "blocks": [{
88: "type": "Table",
89: "bbox": { "page": 1, "left": 0.516, ... },
90: "confidence": "high"
91: }]
92: }]
93: },
94: "studio_link": "https://studio.reducto.ai/..."
95: }
96: ```
97: ## Understanding the response
98: Here's what we got back from parsing our financial statement:
99: ```json
100: {
101: "job_id": "5df31070-8d98-4caa-9a5b-c5c511a03f71",
102: "duration": 11.35,
103: "usage": {
104: "num_pages": 3,
105: "credits": 4.0
106: },
107: "result": {
108: "chunks": [
109: {
110: "content": "# *** SAMPLE STATEMENT ***\nFor informational purposes only\n\nFidelity\nINVESTMENTS\n\n## Your Portfolio Value:\n\n$274,222.20\n\n| | This Period | Year-to-Date |\n|-|-|-|\n| Beginning Portfolio Value | $253,221.83 | $232,643.16 |\n| Additions | 59,269.64 | 121,433.55 |...",
111: "blocks": [
112: {
113: "type": "Title",
114: "content": "*** SAMPLE STATEMENT ***\nFor informational purposes only",
115: "bbox": {"page": 1, "left": 0.351, "top": 0.029, "width": 0.296, "height": 0.057},
116: "confidence": "high"
117: },
118: {
119: "type": "Section Header",
120: "content": "Your Portfolio Value:",
121: "bbox": {"page": 1, "left": 0.517, "top": 0.163, "width": 0.153, "height": 0.015},
122: "confidence": "high"
123: },
124: {
125: "type": "Table",
126: "content": "| | This Period | Year-to-Date |\n|-|-|-|\n| Beginning Portfolio Value | $253,221.83 | $232,643.16 |\n| Additions | 59,269.64 | 121,433.55 |\n| Subtractions | -45,430.74 | -98,912.58 |\n| Transaction Costs, Fees & Charges | -139.77 | -625.87 |\n| Change in Investment Value* | 7,161.47 | 19,058.07 |\n| Ending Portfolio Value** | $274,222.20 | $274,222.20 |",
127: "bbox": {"page": 1, "left": 0.516, "top": 0.261, "width": 0.444, "height": 0.158},
128: "confidence": "high"
129: }
130: ]
131: }
132: ]
133: },
134: "studio_link": "https://studio.reducto.ai/job/5df31070-8d98-4caa-9a5b-c5c511a03f71"
135: }
136: ```
137: **Key fields:**
138: | Field | What it contains |
139: | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
140: | `job_id` | Unique identifier for this job. Use it to retrieve results later or debug in Studio. |
141: | `usage.num_pages` | Number of pages that were processed. |
142: | `usage.credits` | Credits consumed by this request. |
143: | `chunks` | Logical sections of the document, optimized for feeding into LLMs. |
144: | `chunks[].content` | The full text content of this chunk. |
145: | `chunks[].blocks` | Individual elements (tables, headers, text) with their types and positions. |
146: | `blocks[].type` | What kind of element this is: `Title`, `Table`, `Section Header`, `Text`, `Figure`, etc. |
147: | `blocks[].bbox` | Bounding box with normalized coordinates (0-1) showing where this element appears on the page. |
148: | `studio_link` | Direct link to view this job in Reducto Studio for visual debugging. |
149: ---
150: ## Customizing the output
151: r-1 needs no extra settings. The options you may want change the shape of the output, not its quality:
152: ```python
153: result = client.parse.run(
154: input=upload.file_id,
155: settings={"model": "r-1", "page_range": {"start": 1, "end": 5}},
156: formatting={"table_output_format": "html"},
157: retrieval={"chunking": {"chunk_mode": "variable"}},
158: )
159: ```
160: - **`formatting.table_output_format`**: `dynamic` (default), `html`, `md`, `json`, or `csv`.
161: - **`retrieval.chunking.chunk_mode`**: split the output into chunks for RAG.
162: - **`settings.page_range`**: parse only some pages.
163: For word-level bounding boxes, add [Parse citations](/configs/parse/citations). See [Parse options](/parse/overview#options) for the full list.
164: ---
165: ## Fastest path for coding agents
166: If you are using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent, start here. This path avoids Studio clicks and extra docs navigation.
167: 1. Set `REDUCTO_API_KEY`.
168: 2. Choose one interface:
169: - Local file or folder: use the [Reducto CLI](/cli).
170: - Agent tool calling: use the [Reducto MCP server](/mcp-server).
171: - Application code: use the Python, Node.js, Go, or cURL examples below.
172: 3. Parse the sample PDF first, then replace the URL or file path with your document.
173: **CLI**
174: ```bash
175: pip install reducto-cli
176: reducto login
177: curl -L -o fidelity-example.pdf https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf
178: reducto parse ./fidelity-example.pdf
179: ```
180: **Python**
181: ```python
182: from reducto import Reducto
183: client = Reducto()
184: result = client.parse.run(input="https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf", settings={"model": "r-1"})
185: print(result.job_id)
186: print(result.result.chunks[0].content[:1000])
187: ```
188: **Node.js**
189: ```javascript
190: import Reducto from "reductoai";
191: const client = new Reducto();
192: const result = await client.parse.run({
193: input: "https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf",
194: settings: { model: "r-1" },
195: });
196: console.log(result.job_id);
197: console.log(result.result.chunks[0].content.slice(0, 1000));
198: ```
199: **cURL**
200: ```bash
201: curl -X POST "https://platform.reducto.ai/parse" \
202: -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDUCTO_API_KEY" \
203: -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
204: -d '{"input":"https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf","settings":{"model":"r-1"}}'
205: ```
206: > **Tip:** For MCP, install once with `uvx mcp-server-reducto --login`, then ask the agent to call `parse_document(document_url="https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf")`.
207: ---
208: ## Add Reducto MCP Server
209: ### 1. Authenticate (one-time)
210: ```bash
211: uvx mcp-server-reducto --login
212: ```
213: This opens your browser to approve access. Your API key is saved to `~/.reducto/config.yaml`.
214: ### 2. Add to your MCP client
215: **Claude Code:**
216: ```bash
217: claude mcp add reducto -- uvx mcp-server-reducto
218: ```
219: **Claude Desktop**: edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:
220: ```json
221: {
222: "mcpServers": {
223: "reducto": {
224: "command": "uvx",
225: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
226: }
227: }
228: }
229: ```
230: **Cursor**: edit `.cursor/mcp.json`:
231: ```json
232: {
233: "mcpServers": {
234: "reducto": {
235: "command": "uvx",
236: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
237: }
238: }
239: }
240: ```
241: **VS Code**: edit `.vscode/mcp.json`:
242: ```json
243: {
244: "servers": {
245: "reducto": {
246: "command": "uvx",
247: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
248: }
249: }
250: }
251: ```
252: ### 3. Use it
253: The server provides these tools:
254: | Tool | What it does |
255: |------|-------------|
256: | `upload_file` | Upload a local file or URL to Reducto (returns `reducto://` URL) |
257: | `parse_document` | Parse a document into structured text, tables, figures |
258: | `extract_data` | Extract structured JSON from a document using a schema |
259: | `split_document` | Segment a document into labeled sections |
260: | `classify_document` | Categorize a document type |
261: | `edit_document` | Fill forms or modify a PDF/DOCX |
262: **Local files:** Use `upload_file` first, e.g. `upload_file("./report.pdf")`, then pass the returned `reducto://` URL to other tools.
263: **Chain operations:** `parse_document` returns a `job_id`. Pass `jobid://<job_id>` to `extract_data` or `split_document` to skip re-parsing.
264: ---
265: ## What's next
266: Now that you can parse documents, explore the other Reducto endpoints:
267: - [/extract](/api-reference/api/sections/extract/operations/extract): Define a JSON schema and extract specific fields from your documents.
268: - [/split](/api-reference/api/sections/split/operations/split): Divide long documents into sections based on content type.
269: - [/edit](/api-reference/api/sections/edit/operations/edit): Fill PDF forms and modify DOCX documents programmatically.
270: - [/parse (async)](/api-reference/api/sections/parse/operations/parse-async): Process documents asynchronously with webhooks for high-volume workloads.
271: ---
272: ## Troubleshooting
273: **401 Unauthorized error**
274: This means your API key is missing or invalid. Check that the `REDUCTO_API_KEY` environment variable is set correctly and that the key hasn't expired in Studio.
275: **Tables aren't structured correctly**
276: Try `formatting.table_output_format` set to `"html"` or `"json"` for more structured output. If the table needs custom handling, add a table-scoped prompt to `enhance.agentic`, such as `{"scope": "table", "prompt": "Preserve domain-specific notation such as <0.01, ±, and N/A exactly as written."}`.
277: **Content is missing or garbled**
278: r-1 handles scanned documents and low-quality PDFs natively. If the document is password-protected, pass the password in `settings.document_password`. This may also be due to bad metadata polluting the output, in which case, reach out to Reducto support.
279: > **Tip:** Every response includes a `studio_link` that opens the job in Reducto Studio. Use it to visually inspect what was extracted and debug any issues.
280: Source: https://docs.reducto.ai/quickstart/index.mdx

1: ---
2: title: "Reducto MCP Server"
3: description: "Connect AI agents to Reducto via the Model Context Protocol."
4: ---
5: > Documentation Index
6: > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.reducto.ai/llms.txt
7: > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
8: # Reducto MCP Server
9: The Reducto MCP server connects AI agents directly to Reducto. Once installed, agents in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, or any other [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client can classify, parse, extract, split, and edit documents as part of their reasoning loop, without custom integration code.
10: ## Agent quick path
11: If you are setting this up for a coding agent, choose local MCP for local files and hosted MCP for public URLs.
12: **Claude Code**
13: ```bash
14: uvx mcp-server-reducto --login
15: claude mcp add -s user reducto -- uvx mcp-server-reducto
16: ```
17: **Codex**
18: ```toml
19: [mcp_servers.reducto]
20: command = "uvx"
21: args = ["mcp-server-reducto"]
22: ```
23: **Hosted HTTP**
24: ```json
25: {
26: "mcpServers": {
27: "reducto": {
28: "type": "http",
29: "url": "https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp",
30: "headers": {
31: "Authorization": "Bearer your-api-key"
32: }
33: }
34: }
35: }
36: ```
37: After setup, ask the agent to call:
38: ```text
39: parse_document(document_url="https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf")
40: ```
41: For local files, ask the agent to call `upload_file("./document.pdf")` first, then pass the returned `reducto://` URL to `parse_document`.
42: ## What is MCP?
43: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI agents call external tools. An MCP server exposes a set of tools (here, Reducto's APIs) that the agent can invoke as part of its reasoning loop. You install the server once, point your client at it, and the agent figures out which tool to call and how to chain results.
44: If you've never used MCP before, the mental model is simple: you describe what you want in plain English, and the agent decides which Reducto tool to call, when to upload a file, and how to pass results between steps.
45: ## When to use the MCP server
46: Use the MCP server when you want an agent to:
47: - Answer questions about a PDF, spreadsheet, or scanned document inside Claude Desktop or another chat client.
48: - Read documents and write code against the result inside Claude Code, Cursor, or VS Code Copilot.
49: - Run multi-step workflows (parse, then extract, then split) without you writing glue code.
50: - Prototype a Reducto integration by letting the agent show you the right API calls, schemas, and response shapes.
51: For non-agent workflows (scripting, batch jobs, CI), use the [Reducto CLI](/cli) or one of the [SDKs](/sdk/python/overview) instead.
52: ## Quick Start
53: Pick one of two options. The hosted server is fastest to set up. The local server lets agents read files directly from your machine.
54: ### Option A: Hosted server (no install)
55: The hosted server runs at `https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp`. Add this block to your MCP client config and replace `your-api-key` with a key from [studio.reducto.ai/api-keys](https://studio.reducto.ai/api-keys):
56: ```json
57: {
58: "mcpServers": {
59: "reducto": {
60: "type": "http",
61: "url": "https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp",
62: "headers": {
63: "Authorization": "Bearer your-api-key"
64: }
65: }
66: }
67: }
68: ```
69: > **Warning:** The hosted server runs in the cloud, so it cannot read files from your local filesystem. `upload_file` only accepts public URLs through the hosted server. To upload local files directly, use Option B.
70: ### Option B: Local server (runs on your machine)
71: The local server runs via [`uvx`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and accepts local file paths, public URLs, and `reducto://` references.
72: 1. **Install uv**
73: ```bash
74: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
75: ```
76: 2. **Authenticate**
77: ```bash
78: uvx mcp-server-reducto --login
79: ```
80: This opens an OAuth device-code flow in your browser. Once approved, your API key is saved to `~/.reducto/config.yaml` with `chmod 600`.
81: If you already use the [Reducto CLI](/cli), you're authenticated already. The MCP server reads from the same credential file.
82: 3. **Add to your MCP client**
83: ```json
84: {
85: "mcpServers": {
86: "reducto": {
87: "command": "uvx",
88: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
89: }
90: }
91: }
92: ```
93: No API key in the config: the server reads it from `~/.reducto/config.yaml` automatically.
94: To pass the key explicitly instead (for CI or shared machines), use the `env` field:
95: ```json
96: {
97: "mcpServers": {
98: "reducto": {
99: "command": "uvx",
100: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"],
101: "env": { "REDUCTO_API_KEY": "your-api-key" }
102: }
103: }
104: }
105: ```
106: ### Hosted vs local
107: | | Hosted (`mcp.reducto.ai`) | Local (`uvx mcp-server-reducto`) |
108: | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
109: | Install | None | Python 3.11+, `uvx` |
110: | Auth | Bearer token in headers | Browser login or env var |
111: | Local file uploads | Public URLs only | Local paths supported |
112: | Shares creds with `reducto` CLI | No | Yes |
113: | Best for | Web/Studio users, quick demos | Desktop agents, local workflows |
114: ## Client Setup
115: Most MCP clients use the same JSON shape, but the config file location differs.
116: ### Claude Desktop
117: Edit the config file at `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS, or `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows:
118: ```json
119: {
120: "mcpServers": {
121: "reducto": {
122: "command": "uvx",
123: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
124: }
125: }
126: }
127: ```
128: Restart Claude Desktop after saving. Reducto appears in the MCP servers list.
129: ### Claude Code
130: Add to your project's `.mcp.json` to share the server with collaborators, or run `claude mcp add -s user reducto -- uvx mcp-server-reducto` to enable it across all projects (stored in `~/.claude.json`):
131: ```json
132: {
133: "mcpServers": {
134: "reducto": {
135: "command": "uvx",
136: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
137: }
138: }
139: }
140: ```
141: ### Codex
142: Codex uses TOML, not JSON. Edit `~/.codex/config.toml` (or a project-scoped `.codex/config.toml`) to add the local server:
143: ```toml
144: [mcp_servers.reducto]
145: command = "uvx"
146: args = ["mcp-server-reducto"]
147: ```
148: To use the hosted server instead, configure it as a Streamable HTTP server. Set `REDUCTO_API_KEY` in your environment first, then add:
149: ```toml
150: [mcp_servers.reducto]
151: url = "https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp"
152: bearer_token_env_var = "REDUCTO_API_KEY"
153: ```
154: You can also add the local server via the CLI:
155: ```bash
156: codex mcp add reducto -- uvx mcp-server-reducto
157: ```
158: ### Cursor
159: Add to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project root:
160: ```json
161: {
162: "mcpServers": {
163: "reducto": {
164: "command": "uvx",
165: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
166: }
167: }
168: }
169: ```
170: ### VS Code (Copilot)
171: Add to `.vscode/mcp.json` in your project root:
172: ```json
173: {
174: "servers": {
175: "reducto": {
176: "command": "uvx",
177: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
178: }
179: }
180: }
181: ```
182: ### Windsurf
183: Add to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:
184: ```json
185: {
186: "mcpServers": {
187: "reducto": {
188: "command": "uvx",
189: "args": ["mcp-server-reducto"]
190: }
191: }
192: }
193: ```
194: ### HTTP transport (self-hosted)
195: To run the server in HTTP mode for shared use on a single machine:
196: ```bash
197: REDUCTO_API_KEY=your-key \
198: REDUCTO_MCP_TRANSPORT=http \
199: REDUCTO_MCP_PORT=8000 \
200: uvx mcp-server-reducto
201: ```
202: Connect MCP clients to `http://your-host:8000/mcp`.
203: ## Concepts
204: A few small ideas to internalize before reading the tool reference. Most chained operations rely on these.
205: ### Document URL schemes
206: Every `document_url` parameter accepts one of four schemes:
207: | Scheme | Meaning | Where it comes from |
208: | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
209: | `https://` / `http://` | A public URL Reducto can fetch | You provide it |
210: | `reducto://` | A file in Reducto's temporary storage (24-hour TTL) | Returned by `upload_file` |
211: | `jobid://` | A reference to a previous processing job | Returned by `parse_document`, `extract_data`, `split_document`, `classify_document`, `edit_document` |
212: Other schemes (`s3://`, `file://`, raw paths) fail validation. Use `upload_file` to bring local files or other URLs into Reducto.
213: ### Job chaining with `jobid://`
214: Every processing tool returns a `job_id`. Pass `jobid://<job_id>` as `document_url` to a follow-up tool to reuse the work, with no re-upload and no re-parse:
215: ```text
216: upload_file("./report.pdf") → reducto://abc (file_id)
217: parse_document("reducto://abc") → jobid://xyz123 (job_id)
218: extract_data("jobid://xyz123", ...) → reuses parsed text
219: split_document("jobid://xyz123", ...) → reuses parsed text
220: ```
221: This is the cheapest and fastest way to run multiple operations against the same document.
222: ### Response shape
223: Every tool returns a JSON object with a consistent set of fields. A representative parse response:
224: ```json
225: {
226: "job_id": "xyz123",
227: "duration_seconds": 4.1,
228: "studio_link": "https://studio.reducto.ai/jobs/xyz123",
229: "usage": { "num_pages": 12, "credits": 12 },
230: "num_blocks": 42,
231: "block_type_counts": { "Text": 30, "Table": 6, "Figure": 6 },
232: "blocks": [],
233: "next_steps": "Use jobid://xyz123 as document_url for extract_data, split_document, or classify_document."
234: }
235: ```
236: Common fields:
237: - `job_id`: pass to `get_job` later, or chain via `jobid://<job_id>`.
238: - `studio_link`: open in [Reducto Studio](https://studio.reducto.ai) to inspect the result visually.
239: - `usage`: pages and credits consumed.
240: - `next_steps`: a hint the server adds describing the recommended follow-up call.
241: ### Large or async results
242: When a result is too large to inline, the response contains a URL-backed payload:
243: ```json
244: {
245: "job_id": "xyz123",
246: "result_type": "url",
247: "result_url": "https://...",
248: "result_access_warning": "Result content is URL-backed; call get_job(job_id='xyz123') before reading it."
249: }
250: ```
251: When `result_type` is `"url"`, call `get_job(job_id=...)` to fetch the materialized result before reading any fields. Do not read `result` directly.
252: ### Response truncation
253: If a response (typically the `blocks` array from `parse_document`) exceeds `REDUCTO_MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE` (defaults to `50000` characters), the server truncates it and adds:
254: ```json
255: {
256: "truncated": true,
257: "truncation_note": "Response truncated (showing 20 of 150 blocks). Use get_job(job_id='xyz123') for full results, or narrow with page_range."
258: }
259: ```
260: When `truncated` is `true`, call `get_job(job_id=...)` for the full result, or re-run with a narrower `page_range`.
261: ### The `options` escape hatch
262: Most tools accept an `options` parameter for any [Reducto API field](/api-reference/api/sections/parse/operations/parse) not exposed as a top-level argument.
263: - **Top-level params win.** When a top-level argument and `options` set the same key, the top-level value takes precedence. Nested config dicts get a one-level shallow merge.
264: - **JSON strings are accepted.** Some MCP clients struggle to pass nested JSON. `options`, `schema`, and `categories` therefore each accept either a native object or a JSON-encoded string. Both work identically.
265: ### Page range syntax
266: `page_range` accepts a string with **1-based** page numbers:
267: - `"1-5"`: pages 1 through 5
268: - `"3,7,10-12"`: pages 3, 7, 10, 11, and 12
269: ## Tools
270: ### Which tool to use
271: | If you need to... | Use |
272: | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
273: | Look up working SDK or REST examples for any Reducto endpoint | `get_documentation` |
274: | Bring a local file or arbitrary URL into Reducto | `upload_file` |
275: | Get text, tables, figures, and layout from a document | `parse_document` |
276: | Pull specific fields into JSON using a schema | `extract_data` |
277: | Divide a document into named page-range sections | `split_document` |
278: | Categorize a document into one of N labels | `classify_document` |
279: | Fill a form or modify a PDF or DOCX | `edit_document` |
280: | Fetch a full, URL-backed, truncated, or async result | `get_job` |
281: | Inspect recent jobs | `list_jobs` |
282: ### `get_documentation`
283: Returns Reducto SDK and REST documentation, including install commands, auth setup, working code examples, and response shapes for a specific topic. Call this **before** writing any Reducto integration code so the agent works from the current API surface, not training memory.
284: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
285: | ---------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
286: | `topic` | string | Yes | One of: `quickstart`, `parse`, `extract`, `split`, `classify`, `edit`, `upload`, `auth` |
287: | `language` | string | No | `node`, `python`, or `http`. Omit to receive all three. |
288: ### `parse_document`
289: Parses a document into structured text, tables, and figures. Supports PDFs, images, spreadsheets, DOCX, PPTX, and 30+ other formats.
290: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
291: | --------------------- | ------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
292: | `document_url` | string | Yes | `https://`, `reducto://`, or `jobid://` URL |
293: | `table_output_format` | string | No | `html`, `json`, `md`, `csv`, `dynamic`, `jsonbbox` (defaults to `dynamic`) |
294: | `page_range` | string | No | e.g. `"1-5"` or `"3,7,10-12"` (1-based) |
295: | `chunk_mode` | string | No | `disabled`, `variable`, `section`, `page`. See [parse reference](/api-reference/api/sections/parse/operations/parse). |
296: | `agentic` | list[string] | No | Subset of `["text", "table", "figure", "layout"]`. With r-1, use agentic processing for custom prompts or specialized augmentation. Legacy Parse uses it as a general accuracy enhancement. Adds latency. |
297: | `add_page_markers` | bool | No | Insert page-boundary markers in the output |
298: | `return_images` | list[string] | No | Subset of `["figure", "table", "page"]` to return as images |
299: | `options` | dict / JSON string | No | Any other `ParseOptions` field |
300: ### `extract_data`
301: Extracts structured data from a document using a JSON schema.
302: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
303: | --------------- | ------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
304: | `document_url` | string | Yes | Pass `jobid://<parse_job_id>` to skip re-parsing |
305: | `schema` | dict / JSON string | Yes | JSON Schema describing the target fields |
306: | `system_prompt` | string | No | Custom extraction instructions |
307: | `citations` | bool | No | Include source references for each extracted field |
308: | `array_extract` | bool | No | Deprecated flag for repeating items. Prefer `deep_extract`, or model the array directly in your schema. |
309: | `deep_extract` | bool | No | Iterative agentic refinement for harder documents |
310: | `include_images`| bool | No | Add page images to the LLM context |
311: | `page_range` | string | No | Limit pages to process |
312: | `options` | dict / JSON string | No | Any other `ExtractOptions` field |
313: ### `split_document`
314: Segments a document into labeled sections by topic. Returns each section's name, page range, and a confidence score.
315: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
316: | -------------- | ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
317: | `document_url` | string | Yes | Document to split |
318: | `categories` | list / JSON string | Yes | `[{"name": "Disclosures", "description": "Legal and risk disclosures"}, ...]` |
319: | `split_rules` | string | No | Natural-language splitting guidance |
320: | `page_range` | string | No | Limit pages |
321: | `options` | dict / JSON string | No | Any other `SplitOptions` field |
322: ### `classify_document`
323: Categorizes a document into one of the provided categories.
324: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
325: | ------------------- | ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
326: | `document_url` | string | Yes | Document to classify |
327: | `categories` | list / JSON string | Yes | `[{"category": "invoice", "criteria": ["has billing info", "has line items"]}, ...]` |
328: | `page_range` | string | No | Defaults to first 5 pages |
329: | `document_metadata` | string | No | Additional context to bias classification |
330: ### `edit_document`
331: Fills forms or modifies a document (PDF or DOCX). Returns a download URL for the edited file plus a `form_schema` describing the fields it found.
332: The first edit on a new form returns a `form_schema` and a hint:
333: ```json
334: {
335: "document_url": "https://.../edited.pdf",
336: "form_schema": {},
337: "form_schema_note": "Cache this form_schema and pass it via options.form_schema for repeated edits."
338: }
339: ```
340: For repeated edits to the same form template, cache `form_schema` and pass it back via `options.form_schema` to skip re-detection.
341: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
342: | ------------------- | ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------- |
343: | `document_url` | string | Yes | Document to edit |
344: | `edit_instructions` | string | Yes | Natural-language instructions |
345: | `options` | dict / JSON string | No | `edit_options`, `form_schema`, `priority` |
346: ### `upload_file`
347: Uploads a document to Reducto's temporary storage (24-hour TTL) and returns a `reducto://` URL for use in other tools.
348: Accepts:
349: - **Local file paths**: `./report.pdf`, `/Users/me/docs/x.pdf`, `~/inbox/y.pdf` (local server only).
350: - **Public URLs**: `https://example.com/report.pdf` (downloaded server-side, then uploaded).
351: > **Note:** The hosted server (`mcp.reducto.ai`) does not support local paths. Use a public URL or run the server locally.
352: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
353: | ----------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
354: | `file_url` | string | Yes | Local file path or public URL |
355: ### `get_job`
356: Returns the status and result of a previous processing job. Use this to fetch URL-backed results, full content for truncated responses, or to poll an async job.
357: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
358: | -------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
359: | `job_id` | string | Yes | Job ID returned by any processing tool |
360: ### `list_jobs`
361: Returns recent processing jobs.
362: | Name | Type | Required | Description |
363: | ------- | ---- | -------- | -------------------------------------- |
364: | `limit` | int | No | Max jobs to return (defaults to `10`) |
365: ## Usage Patterns
366: ### Basic parse
367: > "Parse this PDF and show me the content."
368: The agent calls `parse_document(document_url="https://example.com/report.pdf")`.
369: ### Extract with a schema
370: > "Extract the invoice number, date, and total from this document."
371: The agent calls `extract_data` with a JSON schema describing the three fields.
372: ### End-to-end chain
373: A full workflow using `upload_file`, `parse_document`, and chained `extract_data`:
374: ```text
375: 1. upload_file("./contracts/q4-msa.pdf")
376: → { "file_id": "reducto://abc", "next_steps": "Pass reducto://abc as document_url ..." }
377: 2. parse_document("reducto://abc")
378: → { "job_id": "xyz123", "studio_link": "...", "next_steps": "Use jobid://xyz123 ..." }
379: 3. extract_data(
380: "jobid://xyz123",
381: schema={
382: "type": "object",
383: "properties": {
384: "effective_date": {"type": "string"},
385: "parties": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
386: "termination_clauses": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
387: },
388: "required": ["effective_date", "parties"]
389: },
390: citations=True
391: )
392: → structured fields, with citations
393: ```
394: The same `jobid://xyz123` can also be reused by `split_document` or `classify_document` without re-parsing.
395: ### Triage a mixed document set
396: > "Classify each of these PDFs as `invoice`, `contract`, or `lab_report`, then run the right extraction schema for each."
397: The agent calls `classify_document` per file, then routes each to `extract_data` with a category-specific schema.
398: ### Fill a recurring form
399: > "Fill out a W-9 for each of these vendors using the data in `vendors.json`."
400: The first call to `edit_document` returns a `form_schema`. Subsequent calls pass the cached `form_schema` via `options` to skip re-detection.
401: ### Handle large or async results
402: If a response includes `result_type: "url"`, call `get_job` before reading fields:
403: ```text
404: parse_document("reducto://big-doc")
405: → { "job_id": "j1", "result_type": "url", "result_url": "...",
406: "result_access_warning": "Result content is URL-backed; call get_job(job_id='j1') before reading it." }
407: get_job(job_id="j1")
408: → full materialized result
409: ```
410: If a response includes `truncated: true`, either call `get_job(job_id=...)` for the full result or re-run with a narrower `page_range`.
411: ## Authentication
412: The server resolves API keys in this order:
413: 1. **`REDUCTO_API_KEY` environment variable** (highest priority). Useful for CI or explicit config.
414: 2. **`~/.reducto/config.yaml`**, the shared credential store with the Reducto CLI.
415: Three ways to authenticate:
416: ```bash
417: # Browser login (recommended)
418: uvx mcp-server-reducto --login
419: # Reuse an existing CLI session
420: reducto login
421: # Set the env var directly
422: export REDUCTO_API_KEY=your-key
423: ```
424: `--login` runs an OAuth device-code flow: it prints a code, opens your browser to the verification page, and waits for you to approve. Once approved, the key is written to `~/.reducto/config.yaml` with `chmod 600`. Use `--login --force` to replace an existing saved key.
425: The hosted server (`mcp.reducto.ai`) does not use this flow. Pass your key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` in your client config instead.
426: ## Environment Variables
427: | Variable | Required | Default | Description |
428: | --------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
429: | `REDUCTO_API_KEY` | No\* | none | API key (or authenticate via `--login`) |
430: | `REDUCTO_BASE_URL` | No | `https://platform.reducto.ai` | Override the API base URL (EU region, on-prem) |
431: | `REDUCTO_MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE` | No | `50000` | Response truncation threshold in characters |
432: | `REDUCTO_MCP_TIMEOUT` | No | `300` | Request timeout in seconds |
433: | `REDUCTO_MCP_TRANSPORT` | No | `stdio` | Transport mode: `stdio` or `http` |
434: | `REDUCTO_MCP_PORT` | No | `8000` | Port when using HTTP transport |
435: | `REDUCTO_TELEMETRY` | No | `1` | Set to `0` to opt out of anonymous usage telemetry |
436: \*Required only if you have not run `mcp-server-reducto --login` or `reducto login`.
437: ## Telemetry
438: The MCP server sends a small amount of anonymous usage telemetry to PostHog so the team can prioritize improvements.
439: Collected:
440: - Lifecycle events: `mcp.installed` (once per machine, on first run) and `mcp.start` (once per server boot).
441: - Per-tool invocation events: `tool.<name>.invoked` with `tool` name, `status` (`ok`, `error`, or `exception`), and `latency_ms`.
442: - Environment fingerprint on every event: client name and version, transport (`stdio` or `hosted`), Python version, OS platform.
443: Never collected:
444: - Tool arguments (document URLs, file IDs, schemas, prompts, page ranges).
445: - Tool responses or document content.
446: - API keys. The user identifier on each event is `sha256(api_key)[:16]`, which is one-way.
447: To opt out, set `REDUCTO_TELEMETRY=0` in the environment that runs the MCP server.
448: ## Debugging
449: ### MCP Inspector
450: Test the server interactively:
451: ```bash
452: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector -- uvx mcp-server-reducto
453: ```
454: This opens a web UI where you can discover tools, call them, and inspect responses. Requires prior authentication via `--login`.
455: ### Studio links
456: Most parse and extract responses include a `studio_link`. Open it to inspect the same job interactively in [Reducto Studio](https://studio.reducto.ai). This is the fastest way to compare parser output side by side with the original document.
457: ### Logs
458: The server logs to stderr. Stdout is reserved for the MCP transport. Set `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` for verbose output.
459: ## Troubleshooting
460: **No Reducto API key found**
461: **Problem**: The server starts but every tool call fails with an authentication error.
462: **Solution**: Run `mcp-server-reducto --login`, or set `REDUCTO_API_KEY` in your client config's `env` block.
463: **Invalid URL scheme**
464: **Problem**: A tool call fails with a validation error about `document_url`.
465: **Solution**: `document_url` must start with `https://`, `http://`, `reducto://`, or `jobid://`. For local files, call `upload_file` first to get a `reducto://` URL.
466: **Local file paths are not supported on the hosted server**
467: **Problem**: You passed a local path to `upload_file` while connected to `mcp.reducto.ai`.
468: **Solution**: Switch to the local server (Option B above), or pass a public URL.
469: **Tools not appearing in the client**
470: **Problem**: After editing your client config, no Reducto tools show up.
471: **Solution**: Restart your MCP client. Then test the server directly by running `uvx mcp-server-reducto` in your terminal to confirm it starts cleanly.
472: **Timeout on large documents**
473: **Problem**: A long-running parse or extract returns a timeout error.
474: **Solution**: Increase `REDUCTO_MCP_TIMEOUT` (defaults to `300` seconds), or narrow the request with `page_range`.
475: **Result not visible in the response**
476: **Problem**: A response references content but the `result` field is empty or missing.
477: **Solution**: Check for `result_type: "url"` or `truncated: true`. In either case, call `get_job(job_id=...)` to fetch the full materialized result.
478: ## Next Steps
479: - [Reducto CLI](/cli): Run parse, extract, and edit from your terminal.
480: - [Agent Guide](/agent-guide): A self-contained API reference designed for AI coding agents.
481: - [Parse Overview](/parse/overview): How parse turns documents into structured text, tables, and figures.
482: - [Extract Overview](/extract/overview): Schema-driven structured data extraction.
483: Source: https://docs.reducto.ai/mcp-server/index.mdx

The main sidebar provides access to Home, Usage, API Keys, Webhooks, and Billing. The sidebar footer contains Documentation, Support, Give Feedback, and Settings. This page covers common account management tasks. 10: --- 11: ## API Keys 12: 13: API keys authenticate your requests to Reducto. Navigate to **API Keys** in the sidebar to manage them. 14: > **Note:** All roles can create API keys. Only **Owners** and **Admins** can edit or delete keys. See [Roles & Permissions](/studio-roles-permissions) for details. 15: To create a new API key: 16: 1. Click **Create API Key** 17: 2. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "production", "staging", "local-dev") 18: 3. Copy the key immediately, you won't be able to see it again 19: The table shows each key's name, prefix, creator, creation date, and expiration. Deleting a key immediately revokes access, and any requests using that key will fail. 20: Organization Owners and Admins are notified by email a week and a day before an API key expires. Rotate keys ahead of their expiration to avoid service disruptions. 21: > **Note:** For security, create separate API keys for different environments (development, staging, production). If a key is compromised, you can revoke it without affecting other environments. 22: --- 23: ## Usage 24: The Usage page tracks your Reducto consumption. Navigate to **Usage** in the sidebar to view your dashboard. 25: 26: ### Usage chart 27: The chart shows usage over time, broken down by product (Parse, Extract, Split, Edit, Classify). The unit on the y axis depends on your pricing model (see the [Pricing Migration Guide](/reference/pricing-migration#which-pricing-model-am-i-on)): 28: - **Pages**: accounts on per-product pricing. The chart shows billable pages, the count Reducto uses for pricing. 29: - **Credits**: accounts on credit-based pricing. The chart shows credits consumed. 30: Use the filters to: 31: - **Group by**: Switch the breakdown. Accounts on per-product pricing can group by Product or API key. Accounts on credit-based pricing can also group by Feature or File type. 32: - **Product / API key**: Filter to specific products or API keys. Accounts on credit-based pricing can also filter by Feature and File type. 33: - **Time range**: View the last 7, 30, or 90 days, or pick a custom range 34: - **Granularity**: Toggle between Day, Week, and Month views 35: Click **Download** to export your usage data. You can also export usage data programmatically via the [Usage Export API](/reference/usage-export-api). 36: ### Request logs 37: Below the chart, the Request Logs table shows individual API requests. Each entry includes: 38: - Job ID 39: - Date and time 40: - Type (Parse, Extract, Split, Edit, Classify) 41: - Page count processed 42: - Status 43: Studio shows jobs from the last 12 hours. Click **Refresh** to load the latest entries. Use the region dropdown to filter by data center (US, EU, etc.). 44: Click the **...** menu on any request to see the full job details, including the exact configuration used. Click **Preview** to recreate that pipeline in a new Studio instance. 45: 46: --- 47: ## Billing 48: Navigate to **Billing** in the sidebar to see your current plan, usage alerts, and billing history. 49: > **Note:** The billing page is only visible for account owners and organizations on a subscription plan. 50: From the Billing page you can: 51: - **View invoices**: See past and upcoming charges under Billing history 52: - **Update payment methods**: Click **Add payment method** 53: - **Manage subscription**: Click **Manage plan** to open the Stripe customer portal 54: - **Download receipts**: Click **View invoices in Stripe** 55: ### Subscription changes 56: Monthly and yearly plans are available. To change your plan, use **Manage plan** or contact [support@reducto.ai](mailto:support@reducto.ai). 57: ### Usage alerts 58: Configure usage alerts from the Billing page to get an email when your current invoice crosses a threshold you set. Click **Create alert** to open the dialog. 59: 60: Each alert has: 61: - **Threshold**: The invoice amount (in USD) that triggers the alert 62: - **Recipients**: The organization members who receive the email 63: - **Label**: An optional name for the alert (e.g., "Budget warning") 64: Reducto compares your current invoice to the threshold every hour. Recipients are emailed once per period when usage crosses the threshold. Editing the threshold re-arms the alert. 65: --- 66: ## Organization Settings 67: The **Settings** page lets you manage your profile and organization. 68: ### Account settings 69: On the **Account** tab, you can: 70: - Edit your name and email 71: - Change your profile picture 72: - Set a password or enable two-factor authentication (2FA) 73: - Choose a theme (Light or Dark) 74: - Manage cookie preferences 75: ### Organization management 76: If you're an organization Owner or Admin, you can: 77: - Invite team members 78: - Manage member roles and permissions 79: See [Roles & Permissions](/studio-roles-permissions) for a full breakdown of what each role can do. 80: --- 81: ## Webhooks 82: Configure webhooks to receive notifications when jobs complete. Navigate to **Webhooks** in the sidebar. 83: Webhooks let you: 84: - Get notified when async jobs finish 85: - Trigger downstream workflows automatically 86: - Avoid polling the API for job status 87: See [Webhook Configuration](/recipes/svix-webhooks) for setup details. 88: --- 89: ## Related 90: - [API Quickstart](/quickstart): Set up your API key and make your first request. 91: - [Credit Usage](/reference/credit-usage): How credits are calculated and billed. 92: - [Webhook Setup](/recipes/svix-webhooks): Configure webhooks for async job notifications. 93: - [Security Policies](/security/policies): Data handling, retention, and compliance information. 94: Source: https://docs.reducto.ai/studio-account/index.mdx
